genZNote: The organism responsible for both the holes and the nutty flavor in Swiss cheese — it eats the lactic acid other bacteria made and burps out CO2 gas bubbles as it goes.

morphology.arrangement: Single cells, chains, V-forms, or clumps

habitat.hostAssociation: Not part of normal human microbiota; used as a food-grade starter/ripening culture
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Central to the production of Swiss-type cheeses (Emmental, Gruyère) during the secondary fermentation/ripening stage

culture.media: Sodium lactate agar or specialized propionibacteria media
culture.growthCharacteristics: Slow-growing aerotolerant anaerobe; ferments lactate to propionic acid, acetic acid, and CO2

biochemicalTests.test: Lactate fermentation to propionic acid + CO2

identificationClues: Ferments lactic acid (produced earlier by starter lactic acid bacteria) into propionic acid, acetic acid, and CO2 — the propionic acid fermentation
The CO2 gas produced during this secondary fermentation forms the characteristic large 'eyes' (holes) of Swiss-type cheeses like Emmental
Contributes the characteristic nutty, sweet flavor notes of Swiss cheese as a byproduct of propionic acid fermentation
Distinct from the skin-associated Cutibacterium acnes (formerly also classified as Propionibacterium) — a useful point for avoiding confusion between the two genera

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Propionic acid fermentation of lactate (produces CO2 + propionic acid + acetic acid)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Produces both the holes and the nutty flavor of Swiss-type cheeses via propionic acid fermentation of lactate
